qs.q: Why is the reaction catalyzed by pyruvate carboxylase considered an anaplerotic reaction for the citric acid cycle?
o: It directly generates ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation
It links carbohydrate catabolism directly to urea synthesis
It removes excess reducing equivalents from the mitochondrial
It provides carbon skeletons exclusively for ketogenesis pathways
It replenishes cycle intermediates drained by biosynthetic pathways
qs.e: Anaplerotic reactions replenish citric acid cycle intermediates that are continuously drawn off for various anabolic pathways.

qs.q: A patient with a rare genetic deficiency in liver pyruvate carboxylase suffers from severe fasting hypoglycemia and lethargy. What is the primary metabolic failure in this condition?
o: Blockade of glycogen breakdown due to defective allosteric activation
Failure to convert acetyl-CoA into ketone bodies during starvation periods
Inability to synthesize oxaloacetate from pyruvate for gluconeogenesis
Incapacitation of the electron transport chain through substrate starvation
Accumulation of toxic levels of lactate within the central nervous system
qs.e: Pyruvate carboxylase is the essential first enzyme of gluconeogenesis that converts pyruvate into oxaloacetate within the mitochondria.

qs.q: An inherited defect impairs pyruvate carboxylase function in a newborn infant. Which metabolic conversion pathway is directly blocked by this specific enzyme deficiency?
o: Pyruvate conversion into acetyl-CoA
Lactate reduction back to pyruvate
Oxaloacetate synthesis from pyruvate
Alanine transamination into pyruvate
Malate oxidation yielding pyruvate
qs.e: Pyruvate carboxylase is a biotin-dependent mitochondrial enzyme that carboxylates pyruvate to form oxaloacetate.

qs.q: A patient with a rare genetic disorder exhibits lactic acidosis and hyperammonemia due to an inherited defect in pyruvate carboxylase. Which metabolic consequence best explains the systemic effects?
o: Accumulated acetyl‑CoA drives increased ketone body synthesis.
Excess pyruvate directly inhibits hepatic urea‑cycle enzymes.
Lack of oxaloacetate impairs gluconeogenesis and TCA cycle flux.
Reduced ATP production limits amino‑acid reabsorption in the kidney.
Enhanced transamination pushes nitrogen into toxic intermediates.
qs.e: Pyruvate carboxylase replenishes oxaloacetate; its deficiency impairs gluconeogenesis and compromises TCA cycle intermediates.
